rationale: The reply gives a clear stop-use, unplug and engineer-inspection message, explains lint and vent blockage as the likely cause alongside a possible electrical fault, and forbids opening the casing. It is repetitive, restating 'switch off and unplug' and the fire risk twice, and it asks no follow-up questions, for example about smoke, scorching, model number or the state of the filter and hose. It also suggests a belt rubbing as a cause, which is less relevant here, but it makes no unsupported claims and recommends no part. Checking the filter and hose is correctly limited to power-off only.</br>
